lede: The most consequential thing happening in local government this week is a San Miguel County special meeting Wednesday where the Housing Authority will vote on Resolution 2026-34, adjusting AMI limits for deed-restricted units at Pinion Park — a quiet but pivotal move that shapes who actually qualifies for workforce housing here. The county Planning Commission also takes up three Land Use Code amendments Thursday covering forestry, oil and gas, and geothermal energy, all headed toward the BOCC if they get a recommendation. Meanwhile, the Film Festival aftermath settles over town as the week finds its rhythm.

notable.stake: Vote on AMI limits for deed-restricted Pinion Park housing units.
Planning Commission recommends on three Land Use Code amendments before BOCC action.
